messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager alert: cross_region_routing_anomaly triggered for route-controller policy-901 (sev2). Paging alex (oncall).
alex: saw the alert, joining. p99 latency spike for ap-southeast -> 1100ms and approx 7% of traffic from eu->ap were routed to us-east. some clients seeing 502s and 403 model-mismatch errors.
maya: checking model pins — ap-southeast currently has model v3.1, us-east still on v3.0. that explains the mismatch for pinned customers.
netops-bot: RouteDiff: policy-901 applied at 11:03:12 UTC. Route table shows unexpected next-hop set to region us-east for prefixes normally pinned to ap-southeast.
chris: did we push any policy changes in the last hour? I ran a quick git log — there was an emergency tweak to default_fallback in the rollout script around 10:55.
emily: dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/policy-901 | logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/q=policy%2D901
alex: I see a rollout job jumped to global default_fallback=true which overrides regional pins when a minor mismatch exists — that's the regression.
ryan: opening cloud support case SR-2109 to check if LB health checks are causing region selection churn.
alex: immediate plan: 1) pause the rollout job, 2) force regional pins for critical regions, 3) flush edge caches and instruct app teams to purge if needed.
incident-bot: RolloutService: pause requested by alex for rollout-3242. Status: pausing...
maya: applying hotfix to policy-901 to force pin for ap-southeast org-wide: ```
routectl set policy-901 regional_overrides.ap-southeast.pin=ap-southeast --force
routectl commit
``` 
alex: executing cache flush for the routing layer and DNS cdn caches: ```
routectl flush --policy policy-901 --scope routing_cache,dns_edge
cdnctl purge /routes/policy-901
``` 
support-ops: note: DNS TTLs for the regional endpoints were 180s, but some ISP caches persist >10m. we'll include cache-purge instructions for customers.
emily: after the pin, p99 in AP region dropped from 1100ms -> 160ms. overall error responses dropped from 7% -> 0.9% in 6m.
chris: can we temporarily divert traffic for enterprise customers to a verified control-plane route to avoid hitting older model nodes? we have a canary pool with v3.1.
alex: enabled enterprise-only routing override to canary pool: ```
routectl add override policy-901 customers=["AcmeCorp","MedPlus"] target=canary-pool-v3.1
``` 
ryan: cloud support responded: no L3/L4 anomalies, load balancer logs show sticky session cookies expired causing some sessions to land on different regional backends; they recommended session affinity tuning.
maya: we'll add a server-side check to reject mismatched model-version requests early to reduce downstream 403 noise and log more context for tracing.
chris: logging action item: correlate client session id -> route decisions so we can replay and find where routing decision flipped.
support-ops: drafting customer communication for impacted accounts. includes timeline, mitigation steps, and recommended client cache flush command for common CDNs.
oncall-next: I'll take over monitoring and keep the thread open. handoff: alex did rollback of the rollout job, forced regional pins, flushed caches, enabled enterprise override. current state: stable with p99 normalizing.
alex: escalation criteria: promote to sev1 if error rate >3% for >10m or p99 >500ms for >10m or >50% of requests misrouted.
emily: creating a post-incident ticket: ENG-PLATFORM-541 with tags: routing, rollout-regression, dns-cache, postmortem-assignee eng-runtime.
chris: I’ll own the regression fix in rollout service to ensure default_fallback doesn't override explicit regional pins. also adding an automated test path.
support-ops: customer notices sent to affected customers. support is triaging any follow-ups.
incident-bot: Incident status updated -> mitigated. owners -> eng-runtime, network. severity -> sev2 (monitoring)
maya: thanks everyone. please add any findings to ENG-PLATFORM-541 and include logs from 11:00-11:30 UTC.
oncall-next: acknowledged. monitoring active. will page the chain if anything regresses.
